• A rider on an early bicycle pushed against the ground with both feet to move  
  forward. The bicycle developed as makers added pedals, better wheels, and     
  safer frames to this simple idea.                                             
                                                                                
  In 1817, German inventor Karl von Drais built a two-wheeled machine that    
  riders moved with their feet. It had a wooden frame and a front wheel that  
  could turn. It had no pedals, but it showed that a person could balance on two
  wheels in line.
